handoffs.message: Helper-claimed by Copilot while Claude completes higher-priority work.
Helper-claimed by Codex2 while Codex completes higher-priority work.
QuantLib governed adapter delivered: adapter package, smoke test, and 17 passing unit tests. Checklist advanced to smoke-tested on 2026-04-17; ready for review.

Review changes requested: QuantLibBackend American-option finite-difference Greeks are mis-scaled at services/research/quantlib/adapter/quantlib_adapter.py:288-312. With vol_bump=0.01 and rate_bump=0.0001, current code returns materially understated vega/rho (local check on the same option: base _bs_metrics vega/rho=1.018182/0.974281 vs _finite_difference_greeks=0.010213/0.000097). Please fix the scaling to match the European-path per-1% conventions and add coverage for the real/American path before re-handoff.

Fixed American finite-difference Greek scaling: vega now reports per-1% vol and rho now converts 1bp bump to per-100bp convention. Added QuantLibBackend American-path test coverage with conditional skip when QuantLib is unavailable; verification: python3 -m pytest services/research/quantlib/test_adapter.py -q => 17 passed, 1 skipped, and python3 services/research/quantlib/smoke_test.py => OK.

Review changes requested: QuantLibBackend still returns mixed-model American analytics. services/research/quantlib/adapter/quantlib_adapter.py:273-311 prices American options with binomial CRR NPV but derives delta/gamma/vega/theta/rho from _bs_metrics(), which is a European Black-Scholes proxy and never bumps the American QuantLib engine. The new regression test at services/research/quantlib/test_adapter.py:176-188 only compares against the same proxy, so it cannot catch this mismatch. Either compute bumped Greeks from the same American QuantLib pricing path or reject/explicitly gate American style until supported, then refresh tests and return to review.

Reworked QuantLibBackend American analytics to use the same binomial CRR pricing path for NPV and finite-difference Greeks instead of mixing in _bs_metrics(). Added an independent QuantLib-backed regression test that computes expected American Greeks from bumped binomial NPV paths and asserts they diverge from the BS proxy fixture. Verification: python3 -m pytest services/research/quantlib/test_adapter.py -q => 17 passed, 1 skipped (QuantLib not installed in this workspace); python3 services/research/quantlib/smoke_test.py => OK.

Review changes requested: independent live rerun with pinned QuantLib-Python==1.18 found a real blocker. PYTHONPATH=/tmp/oss-impl-002-site python3 -m pytest services/research/quantlib/test_adapter.py -q fails at services/research/quantlib/test_adapter.py:282 because abs(expected['vega'] - baseline['vega']) is 0.009012, not > 0.01. QuantLibBackend output itself matches the bumped binomial engine expectation; the unstable part is the new proxy-divergence assertion, not the pricing path. Please make that regression stable against live QuantLib results, refresh evidence accordingly, and return to review.

Adjusted the American QuantLib regression to assert stable binomial-engine parity plus non-proxy behavior without a brittle vega > 0.01 threshold. Refreshed QuantLib checklist evidence. Verification: python3 -m pytest services/research/quantlib/test_adapter.py -q => 17 passed, 1 skipped; python3 services/research/quantlib/smoke_test.py => OK; PYTHONPATH=/tmp/oss-impl-002-site python3 -m pytest services/research/quantlib/test_adapter.py -q => 18 passed; PYTHONPATH=/tmp/oss-impl-002-site python3 services/research/quantlib/smoke_test.py --backend real => OK.
Review approved: QuantLib governed adapter, smoke coverage, and the revised American regression all verified. Owner may finalize to done.
